name: What to Do About Lingering Smoke Odor After a House Fire

step.name: Step 1
step.text: Dealing with that lingering smoke smell after a fire can feel overwhelming, but there are definite steps you can take to tackle it. First, vent your home as much as possible by opening windows and using fans to circulate fresh air. Next, remove any visibly smoke-damaged items that can't be cleaned, like heavily charred furniture or textiles. Focus on cleaning all hard surfaces with a good quality cleaner, as soot can be greasy and acidic. Don't forget to wash all soft furnishings, curtains, and even clothing. For those really tough, embedded smells, you'll need to go beyond basic cleaning. Consider professional-grade air scrubbers or specialized odor counteractants. The key is thoroughness – smoke particles are sneaky! Sometimes, though, the odor is so deeply absorbed that it requires industrial-strength methods and equipment, like ozone generators or thermal foggers.
